questions.q: A planner wants children to walk safely from their homes to school. Which improvement would help most?
What does "land use" describe?
a: The type of soil on an island
How different areas of land are used

questions.q: A neighbourhood contains homes, shops, offices, and cafés within walking distance. What type of planning is this?
It rains heavily and suddenly the entire street becomes a swimming pool. What did the planner probably forget?
Why might planners avoid placing a school beside a busy industrial area?
a: Noise, pollution, and heavy traffic could affect students

questions.q: What is one advantage of having shops and services close to homes?
a: People are able to walk or cycle for more trips

questions.q: A neighbourhood has 200 parking spaces but ZERO trees. What is a planner most likely to hear from residents?
A street is comfortable for cars but difficult for children, older people, and wheelchair users. What planning principle is missing?
Which change would make a residential street safer without completely banning vehicles?
Why might a planner collect information about how many people walk, cycle, drive, or take buses?
A playground is surrounded by roads with no safe crossings. What should planners consider first?
Why is public consultation useful before redesigning a neighbourhood?
a: Planners learn how people use the area and what problems they face
It removes the need for engineers

questions.q: During heavy rain, water remains on a road for several hours. Which issue is most likely?
Which surface produces the most stormwater runoff during rain?
Why do permeable surfaces help reduce flooding?
a: They allow some water to soak into the ground

questions.q: What is one risk of throwing rubbish into storm drains?
Why is groundwater on small islands vulnerable to pollution?
a: It sits hundreds of metres underground
Pollutants from the surface can reach the shallow freshwater lens

questions.q: What is saltwater intrusion?
Which combination gives an island a more resilient freshwater system?
a: Rainwater collection, groundwater protection, and desalination

questions.q: Why should new developments include drainage planning before construction?
a: Buildings and roads change how rainwater flows

questions.q: A low area regularly floods after rain. Which solution is most appropriate to investigate?
Why does climate-resilient planning matter in Maldives?
a: Low-lying islands face risks from flooding, erosion, heat, and sea-level rise

questions.q: What is coastal erosion?
a: The gradual loss or movement of coastal sand and land

questions.q: Why might removing large amounts of beach sand cause problems?
a: It can change the beach and increase erosion

questions.q: Coral reefs help Maldivian islands in several ways. Which is one important function?
a: Reducing some wave energy before it reaches the coast

questions.q: Why should boats use designated moorings near coral reefs?
a: They reduce damage caused by anchors landing on coral

questions.q: What does biodiversity describe?
a: The variety of plants, animals, and other living organisms
The number of roads on an island

questions.q: Why might planners protect a wetland rather than fill it for construction?
a: Wetlands can provide habitat and store water

questions.q: Which activity is most likely to damage a coral reef directly?
What is an ecosystem service?
a: A service provided by a construction company
A benefit people receive from healthy natural systems

questions.q: Mangroves and wetlands can help an island by:
a: Providing wildlife habitat and helping manage water

questions.q: A developer proposes filling an environmentally important wetland. What should happen before a decision is made?
a: Environmental impacts and alternatives should be assessed
The area should become a car park

questions.q: Which action is highest in the waste hierarchy?
What is source segregation?
a: Separating different types of waste where they are produced

questions.q: Which choice creates the least waste?
a: Using a new plastic cup each time
Throwing away a bottle after one sip

questions.q: Why should batteries be kept separate from ordinary household waste?
a: They contain materials that need special handling

questions.q: Which material is most suitable for composting?
What is the main idea of a circular economy?
a: Keep materials and products in use for as long as practical

questions.q: Why does separating food waste from other rubbish help?
a: Food waste can be treated through options such as composting

questions.q: A café changes from disposable cups to washable cups. Which waste strategy is this closest to?
Why is dumping waste near the shoreline risky?
a: Wind and water can carry pollution into the ocean

questions.q: Which situation best represents responsible waste management?
a: Mixing batteries, food, glass, and plastic
Reducing waste and separating materials for appropriate treatment

questions.q: Why might a heavily paved neighbourhood feel hotter than a shaded green area?
a: Buildings and paved surfaces absorb and release heat

questions.q: What is the "urban heat island" effect?
a: An island created by volcanic heat
Built-up areas becoming warmer than greener surrounding areas

questions.q: Which street design would give pedestrians the best protection from midday heat?
a: Shaded footpaths with suitable trees or structures

questions.q: Why should planners think carefully about where large trees are planted?
a: Trees should always be placed in the middle of roads
Every tree needs the same amount of space
Roots, branches, utilities, footpaths, and buildings all need enough space

questions.q: A coconut palm grows beside a busy playground. Which maintenance issue deserves special attention?
a: The risk of falling coconuts and dead fronds

questions.q: What does "active transport" mean?
a: Ways of travelling using physical activity, such as walking and cycling

questions.q: Which change is most likely to reduce the need for short car or motorcycle trips?
a: Locating daily services within walking distance

questions.q: Why do planners use maps when designing an island?
a: To decide what music people listen to
To see where homes, roads, parks, services, and environmental areas are located
To measure how salty food is

questions.q: Planners want to build a new park. Which information would be most useful?
a: Where people live, pedestrian routes, existing trees, drainage, and nearby facilities

questions.q: You are planning a new neighbourhood in Maldives. Which proposal shows the strongest overall planning approach?
a: Maximise buildings and use remaining land for roads
Combine homes and services with safe walking, drainage, shade, public spaces, waste systems, and environmental protection
Build roads first and consider drainage later

fun.q: You get unlimited money to create ONE public space for teenagers. What do you build?
If you could give an urban planner ONE superpower, what would you choose?
What is more important in a city?
You have one tiny piece of land left in a crowded neighbourhood. What would YOU rather put there?

warmup.s: Let's put the school next to the busiest highway.
Let's make sure everyone can walk safely to the park.
Let's remove all the trees because they take up parking space.
Let's build first and figure out drainage later.
Let's put everything people need within walking distance.
